segments.t: Breathless from his taxi ride, Baek Seung-chan finally reaches the restaurant just as Youn Yuh-jung confronts Ra Joon-mo for sending a brand-new rookie in his place. Once the veteran actress leaves, Joon-mo turns all his frustration onto Seung-chan's roundabout speech. Listen for "dolgorae", 'dolphin', and "hwanyeonghoe", the office welcome party.
드라마나 영화 쪽에서 뵙고 싶다고 그랬습니다.
그냥 나한테 아무 말도 하지 마.
Let's unpack this fiery confrontation one line at a time.

'Did you pass the news to me through that rookie kid?' Calm and piercing, Yuh-jung calls Seung-chan "sinibae", 'newcomer kid', followed by "tonghaeseo", 'through', and "jeondalhada", 'to deliver a message'.
'I have no excuse to offer.' "Deuril malsseumi eopsseumnida" literally says 'there are no humble words to give you' — a set Korean expression admitting complete fault without arguing back.
'Am I an object?' Upset at hearing Joon-mo say he tried to 'handle' the situation, Yuh-jung asks "naega mulgeonini", built around "mulgeon", an inanimate 'thing' or 'piece of merchandise'.
'I am truly sorry.' All Joon-mo can repeat is "joesonghamnida", keeping his head bowed in formal apology.
'You should tell a person yourself.' Before walking out, Yuh-jung stresses "jikjeop", meaning 'in person' or 'firsthand', reminding him that hard news belongs face-to-face.
'What on earth did you say to her?' Once alone with Seung-chan, Joon-mo snaps with "dodaeche", 'on earth' or 'possibly', sharpening "mworago yaegihaennya", 'what did you say?'.
드라마나 영화 쪽에서 뵙고 싶다고 그랬습니다.
'I said I hoped to see her in dramas or movies.' Nervously polite, Seung-chan pairs "deurama", 'TV drama', and "yeonghwa", 'movie', reporting his own roundabout compliment with "boepgo sipdago".
'I said the team needed a change.' Here "byeonhwa" means 'change', linked with "piryohada", 'to be necessary' — far too gentle for anyone to guess she was being replaced.
'Hey, are we dolphins?' Exploding in disbelief, Joon-mo shouts "uriga dolgoraenya", using "dolgorae", 'dolphin', to ask if the crew is supposed to read ultrasonic hints.
'How can anyone catch on if you talk like that?' "Geureoke malhaeseo" means 'speaking in that roundabout way', while "aradeureo" comes from "aradeutda", 'to understand what someone actually means'.
'I'm telling you I don't welcome you.' Refusing to attend the rookie welcome drinks, Joon-mo negates "hwanyeonghada", 'to welcome', sealing it with emphatic "-dago".
그냥 나한테 아무 말도 하지 마.

'Just don't say anything at all to me.' "Amu maldo", 'any words at all', joins "haji ma", 'don't do it' — an order Seung-chan will soon take far too literally. Now let's listen to the whole confrontation again without pauses.
드라마나 영화 쪽에서 뵙고 싶다고 그랬습니다.
그냥 나한테 아무 말도 하지 마.
From "jikjeop" for speaking in person to "aradeutda" for catching someone's real meaning, those expressions pack plenty of punch. Catch you next time!
